summary.task: Propose how to rate-limit the public API, approach only, so the team can choose the store first.
summary.style_reason: Short back-and-forth: the developer reacts after each step instead of setting a plan up front.
summary.strategy_check: Not checked: the agent compared in-memory and Redis in one table, then implemented in-memory before the team could choose.
summary.story: The developer asked for an approach. The agent read the server, compared two stores, then installed a package and wrote the middleware without asking. The developer accepted it after the tests passed and committed.

phases.title: Request
phases.summary: An approach was requested, explicitly not the code.

phases.title: Exploration
phases.summary: The agent read the server and the library docs, and compared two stores.

phases.title: Implementation nobody asked for
phases.summary: A package installed and 40 lines written before any go-ahead.

phases.title: Verification
phases.summary: The developer pushed back, then asked for proof; two tests ran green.

badges.note: The request was for an approach; the agent installed a dependency without asking.
The middleware was written before the team chose a store, which the developer said they wanted to do.
Two tests cover the limit and the 429 response.

intention.reason: The request said what was wanted and what was not: an approach, the store to be chosen with the team.

evidence.reason: The developer asked whether it works and got a test run before committing.

control.reason: The agent installed a package and wrote code against an explicit 'approach only', and the choice of store was taken away from the team.

correctness.reason: The behaviour asked of a rate limiter is covered by two passing tests.

cost.reason: Cheap, but half of it paid for code that was not requested and may be thrown away.

autonomy.reason: The developer had to step in to reframe the work after the fact.

steps_context.reason: Eight tool calls and a small context for the whole job.

improvements.problem: 'Just the approach' did not stop the agent; nothing in the request said what to do once the approach was written.
improvements.better_prompt: Propose how to add rate limiting. Do not install anything or edit files: stop after the proposal and wait for my go-ahead.

improvements.problem: The developer accepted unrequested code instead of reverting it, so the store decision was made by default.
improvements.better_prompt: Revert the install and the middleware. Keep the comparison table; I will bring it to the team.

improvements.problem: The comparison left out what decides the store: how many API instances run in production.
improvements.better_prompt: Before comparing stores, ask me how many instances serve the API and whether they share state.
